96:**PB-10 — Real WebM and MKV files import, play in sync, scrub and export**
97:- **Do:** 1. Get three real files: a YouTube VP9 WebM (e.g. from `yt-dlp -f 'bv*[ext=webm]+ba[ext=webm]'`), a Chrome screen recording (a page using `MediaRecorder`, or any site that saves a `.webm` recording) and an OBS recording saved as MKV with sound. On an M3 or later Mac, also an AV1 WebM. Make a Vorbis WebM beside them: `ffmpeg -f lavfi -i testsrc2=size=640x360:duration=10 -f lavfi -i sine=frequency=440:duration=10 -c:v libvpx-vp9 -c:a vorbis -strict -2 -ac 2 v.webm`. 2. Drop each into a project with no ffmpeg setting changed, and place it. 3. Play it, scrub across it and step with ← and →. 4. Export the project as H.264 and play the export.
98:- **Expect:** each imports with no question and no alert, as a `.mov` under `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/Rewrapped/`. It plays with its sound in sync, every scrub and step shows a picture, and the export plays in sync. The Vorbis WebM imports the same way and plays with its sound in sync.
256:- **Do:** 1. Close every document so Welcome shows, then open Frame Job ▸ Settings…. 2. In a project: File ▸ Export…, Clip ▸ Speed…, Clip ▸ Remove Silences…, Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…, File ▸ Generate Captions…, File ▸ Consolidate Media…, File ▸ New Recording…, Window ▸ Export Queue. 3. In each, hover every button, press and hold one, and look at a disabled one (Settings' Remove with no key set).
271:## Sound and export
285:- **Expect:** the export sits level with the commercial material; the mixed-format track plays clean, at the right pitch, with no gap. (The scripted half is HS-3.) The meter follows what plays: none of the AAC's level stays lit once the WAV plays, and a finished track adds nothing.
294:**SE-5 — Export remembers, queues, and plays**
295:- **Do:** 1. Export with a non-default format, size, quality and loudness; quit and relaunch; open Export… again. 2. Save a user preset, change settings, pick the preset. 3. Start two exports; Window ▸ Export Queue. 4. Save Frame… (⌥⌘E) at a paused frame. 5. Open an exported movie in QuickTime Player. 6. Ask the Assistant to export the project, allow it, and open Window ▸ Export Queue; press its row's Cancel.
296:- **Expect:** the sheet reopens on the last choices and the preset restores them; the queue is listed once, with per-row progress and Cancel; the saved frame matches the preview; the movie plays in QuickTime with sound; the Assistant's export is a row in the queue with its progress, and Cancel stops it.
305:**SE-7 — The ×1000 preview and export**
307:- **Expect:** the preview does NOT keep up (B52a measured 14 of 936 frames and a 30 s stall) and the export takes a long time (about 25 minutes for 32 s in B52a's run), but the export finishes and plays.
308:- **Answer:** are the ×1000 preview and export acceptable as they are (the owner's later test, spec §11 #190)?
318:- **Do:** 1. Set the Document tab's Background opacity to 0 on a project with a title; read the note under it at the inspector's narrowest width. 2. Export… ▸ HEVC with Alpha (MOV); read the footnote on its own line above the sheet's buttons, then rest the pointer on it. 3. Export it, and export the same project as ProRes 4444 (MOV). Play the HEVC file in a Safari page with a coloured background; open each file in QuickTime Player, and lay each over a clip in Final Cut.
319:- **Expect:** the note reads "Transparent — kept by 3 export formats." uncut; the footnote reads "HEVC_ALPHA · MOV · alpha" whole, on a line of its own above the buttons, and resting the pointer on it shows the same line; for both files, the title's edges are clean in every player, with no dark fringe and no line at the frame's edge.
323:- **Do:** 1. Record one take on a camera (its own microphone) and a separate recorder at once, starting them a few seconds apart; clap once near the start. 2. Import both, put the camera clip on one track and the recorder on another anywhere, select both and choose Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio. 3. Mute the camera clip's audio and play the start, the middle and the end of the take; then unmute it and listen to the two together. 4. Try it on a take longer than 10 minutes, and on two clips that are not the same take. 5. On the long take, select the recorder and read its speed in the inspector; export the timeline and watch the end of the exported file too. 6. Trim a long recorder clip so its speech sits near the camera's (as on a real project, within a second or two), then Synchronize Audio. 7. Put both clips at 0:00 where the recorder's matching sound comes later in its file than the camera's, and Synchronize Audio. 8. Select two clips that are not the same take — two takes of the same words, if you have them, each trimmed to the same sentence — and Synchronize Audio.
325:- **Answer:** does the result line up by eye and ear at the start, middle and end of a long take, in playback and in the export, does the corrected recorder sound clean, does a trimmed or head-trimmed recorder line up, and does the refusal's list read sensibly?
345:- **Source:** #298 phase 2, spec §11 SY-23..SY-27 (the export is pinned by `export_offset_proof.py`; the preview's output latency and a 44.1 kHz device are not measured).
348:- **Do:** on a clip of speech set ×0.9995, ×0.9 and ×1.5 with Keep pitch on, play each and export each.
360:- **Do:** set a 60 s clip of speech to ×4 with Keep pitch off; play it at once, then play it again; export it and play the export.

91:**PB-9 — A VP9 MP4 plays, in sync, and scrubs**
92:- **Do:** 1. Make a VP9 MP4 with sound, e.g. `ffmpeg -f lavfi -i testsrc2=size=1280x720:rate=30:duration=10 -f lavfi -i sine=frequency=440:duration=10 -c:v libvpx-vp9 -pix_fmt yuv420p -c:a aac vp9.mp4`, or use a VP9 download from the web in an MP4. 2. Drop it into a project and place it. 3. Play it in the preview, then scrub the playhead across it and step with ← and →.
97:- **Do:** 1. Get three real files: a YouTube VP9 WebM (e.g. from `yt-dlp -f 'bv*[ext=webm]+ba[ext=webm]'`), a Chrome screen recording (a page using `MediaRecorder`, or any site that saves a `.webm` recording) and an OBS recording saved as MKV with sound. On an M3 or later Mac, also an AV1 WebM. Make a Vorbis WebM beside them: `ffmpeg -f lavfi -i testsrc2=size=640x360:duration=10 -f lavfi -i sine=frequency=440:duration=10 -c:v libvpx-vp9 -c:a vorbis -strict -2 -ac 2 v.webm`. 2. Drop each into a project with no ffmpeg setting changed, and place it. 3. Play it, scrub across it and step with ← and →. 4. Export the project as H.264 and play the export.
111:**PB-13 — An MKV the ffmpeg step converts copies its VP9 video, keeps its own name and steps frame by frame**
365:**SE-17 — An AV1 export plays and comes back in**
366:- **Do:** on a Mac with an M3 or later, export a project with sound and motion as AV1 (MP4) at each Speed; play each file in QuickTime Player; import one into a new Frame Job project and play it.
368:- **Answer:** does the AV1 export play in QuickTime and come back into Frame Job, picture and sound in sync?
369:- **Source:** #377, codec-export C1 (spec §11 CX-10, CX-12).
371:**SE-18 — An AV1 (WebM) export plays in the browsers and comes back in**
372:- **Do:** 1. Export a project with sound, motion and two chapter markers as **AV1 (WebM)** from File ▸ Export…. 2. Open the file in Chrome and in Firefox, play it through and scrub it. 3. On a Mac with an M3 or later, import it into a new Frame Job project, put it on the timeline and play it.
375:- **Source:** #377, codec-export C3 (spec §11 CX-6, CX-7, CX-15); `tools/proof/webm_export_proof.py` reads the file through ffprobe, ffmpeg and an EBML walk on an M2 Max, which cannot decode AV1, not how a browser plays it.
377:**SE-19 — A VP9 (WebM) export plays in the browsers and comes back in on another Mac**
378:- **Do:** 1. Export a project with sound, motion and two chapter markers as **VP9 (WebM)** from File ▸ Export…. 2. In an HLG project (Document tab ▸ Dynamic Range ▸ HDR (HLG)) with an iPhone HLG clip, export **VP9 (WebM)** at Dynamic Range HDR (HLG). 3. Open both files in Chrome, Firefox and Safari, play each through and scrub it. 4. On another Apple silicon Mac (an M1 or M2 if one is at hand), import both into a new Frame Job project, put each on the timeline and play it.
379:- **Expect:** every browser plays the 8-bit file's picture and Opus sound in sync to the end, with no corruption, no click at the start or the end, and seeking lands where it is asked; the HLG file (10-bit, VP9 Profile 2) plays in each browser that decodes Profile 2, its highlights not washed out or clipped flat on an HDR display, and a browser that cannot play it says so rather than showing a broken picture; Frame Job on the other Mac imports both, previews them and plays their sound in sync.
380:- **Answer:** do both VP9 files play in Chrome, Firefox and Safari, and come back into Frame Job on another Apple silicon Mac, picture and sound in sync? Which browser, if any, did not play the HLG file?
381:- **Source:** #377, codec-export C4 (spec §11 CX-16); `tools/proof/vp9_export_proof.py` reads the files through ffprobe, ffmpeg and an EBML walk and re-imports them on the M2 Max that builds Frame Job, not how a browser or another Mac plays them.
760:- **Do:** 1. Import an HDR10 PQ file whose mastering peak is above 1,000 cd/m² and whose stated peak you know (a Resolve export, a camera's HDR10 recording or a downloaded HDR10 sample; ideally one at 4,000 cd/m²) into an ordinary (SDR) project of its own. 2. Select its row in the Media tab and read the HDR10 section. 3. Look at its brightest part — a sky, a lamp, a specular highlight — in the preview, paused and playing, and in a saved frame (File ▸ Save Frame…), side by side with the same file in QuickTime Player. 4. Set Peak to 1,000 cd/m², look at the same highlights again, then press Use File's. 5. Undo and redo each step once. 6. If you have one, import an HDR10 file mastered at 1,000 cd/m² or below and repeat 2–3. 7. On an M3 or later Mac, import an HDR10 AV1 file (MP4 or WebM) whose stated peak you know, and an HDR10 VP9 WebM if you have one, and repeat 2. Repeat 2 in the other appearance.
761:- **Expect:** the section reads "Mastered at <its peak> cd/m² (MaxCLL, from the file)" (or "(mastering display, from the file)"), the number the file's maker states, and Peak shows it; the highlights roll off smoothly toward white with their gradation kept — the clouds in a bright sky, the shape of a lamp — rather than flattening into a clipped white patch; at 1,000 cd/m² the brightest parts clip to white sooner, and Use File's brings the gradation back; each change is one undo step named PQ Peak and the clip's timeline filmstrip and Media-tab thumbnail follow it; a 1,000 cd/m² (or lower) file looks as it did before this change; the AV1 and VP9 files' sections read their stated peaks too; the section, the field and its line read clearly in both appearances. Frame Job's picture need not match QuickTime Player's (Apple's own conversion ignores the file's peak, spec §11 HD-6), but it should not look clipped or grey where QuickTime's does not.
762:- **Source:** the HDR road map's H-1 (spec §11 HD-6, HD-12: the peak read at import, the override, step 0's shoulder at the file's peak, #281) and clean-up batch 2 (spec §11 HD-18: the WebM/Matroska Colour element and AV1's metadata OBUs, #316; step 7); `tools/proof/hdr_proof.py`'s H7 family, H7w and P10 measure synthetic x265, AVAssetWriter, libvpx-vp9 and libsvtav1 ramps against an oracle (P10 without a decode: an M1 or M2 Mac refuses AV1 imports), not how a real mastered file's highlights look.
774:**HDR-8 — AV1 and VP9 HDR exports**
## Sound and export

**SE-1 — M3's inspector sections and sheets**
- **Do:** 1. ⌘G and ⇧⌘G (Nest / Un-nest). 2. Turn on the Clip tab's Reverse for a long clip; Cancel the progress sheet; reverse again to the end. 3. Try the Filters, Spotlight, Reflection, Noise Reduction and Compressor sections. 4. Open Export… and look at the Quality row.
- **Expect:** each works and reads cleanly; Cancel stops the reverse and leaves the clip as it was.
- **Source:** #51.

**SE-2 — The level meter, mono and pan**
- **Do:** 1. Play speech and music; watch the meter. 2. In the Audio inspector's Mix section, turn on Mix to Mono for a stereo clip. 3. Sweep its Pan from left to right while playing.

- **Do:** set a 60 s clip of speech to ×4 with Keep pitch off; play it at once, then play it again; export it and play the export.
- **Expect:** the first play has a few seconds of silence, then clean ×4 tape-pitch sound with no click; the second play has sound from the start; the export sounds the same.
- **Answer:** after the brief silence, does the ×4 speech sound clean, and does the export match?
- **Source:** #334, spec §11 SR-28.

**SE-17 — An AV1 export plays and comes back in**
- **Do:** on a Mac with an M3 or later, export a project with sound and motion as AV1 (MP4) at each Speed; play each file in QuickTime Player; import one into a new Frame Job project and play it.
- **Expect:** each file plays in QuickTime with its picture and sound in sync and no corruption, and Frame Job imports it, previews it and plays its sound in sync.
- **Answer:** does the AV1 export play in QuickTime and come back into Frame Job, picture and sound in sync?
- **Source:** #377, codec-export C1 (spec §11 CX-10, CX-12).

**SE-18 — An AV1 (WebM) export plays in the browsers and comes back in**
- **Do:** 1. Export a project with sound, motion and two chapter markers as **AV1 (WebM)** from File ▸ Export…. 2. Open the file in Chrome and in Firefox, play it through and scrub it. 3. On a Mac with an M3 or later, import it into a new Frame Job project, put it on the timeline and play it.
- **Expect:** both browsers play the picture and the Opus sound in sync to the end, with no corruption, no click at the start or the end, and seeking lands where it is asked; on the M3 or later Frame Job imports it, previews it and plays its sound in sync.
- **Answer:** does the WebM play in Chrome and Firefox, and come back into Frame Job on an M3 or later, picture and sound in sync?
- **Source:** #377, codec-export C3 (spec §11 CX-6, CX-7, CX-15); `tools/proof/webm_export_proof.py` reads the file through ffprobe, ffmpeg and an EBML walk on an M2 Max, which cannot decode AV1, not how a browser plays it.

**SE-19 — A VP9 (WebM) export plays in the browsers and comes back in on another Mac**
- **Do:** 1. Export a project with sound, motion and two chapter markers as **VP9 (WebM)** from File ▸ Export…. 2. In an HLG project (Document tab ▸ Dynamic Range ▸ HDR (HLG)) with an iPhone HLG clip, export **VP9 (WebM)** at Dynamic Range HDR (HLG). 3. Open both files in Chrome, Firefox and Safari, play each through and scrub it. 4. On another Apple silicon Mac (an M1 or M2 if one is at hand), import both into a new Frame Job project, put each on the timeline and play it.
- **Expect:** every browser plays the 8-bit file's picture and Opus sound in sync to the end, with no corruption, no click at the start or the end, and seeking lands where it is asked; the HLG file (10-bit, VP9 Profile 2) plays in each browser that decodes Profile 2, its highlights not washed out or clipped flat on an HDR display, and a browser that cannot play it says so rather than showing a broken picture; Frame Job on the other Mac imports both, previews them and plays their sound in sync.
- **Answer:** do both VP9 files play in Chrome, Firefox and Safari, and come back into Frame Job on another Apple silicon Mac, picture and sound in sync? Which browser, if any, did not play the HLG file?
- **Source:** #377, codec-export C4 (spec §11 CX-16); `tools/proof/vp9_export_proof.py` reads the files through ffprobe, ffmpeg and an EBML walk and re-imports them on the M2 Max that builds Frame Job, not how a browser or another Mac plays them.

deleted and the queue carries on; `remove` refuses a job that has not
       finished and takes ONE that has; and `clearFinished` then drops the row
       it left behind. **That last pair is one probe run and the order inside
       it is the check** — it removed BOTH finished rows before the clear
       until the review, so the clear ran over an empty list and answered 0
       whatever its body did.
    5  **the Document tab's transparency note** — the one thing in this phase
       that IS in the editor's own content view, and so the one real
       photograph here.

**The byte claims of section 4 are made over `apng`, and the reason is
measured.** A QuickTime movie carries a creation and a modification time at
one-second resolution: two ProRes 4444 exports of one unchanged project came
back 207,679 bytes each and differed in exactly SIX bytes, all inside the movie
header's time fields, when they landed in different seconds — and were
byte-identical when they landed in the same one. So a byte comparison of two
`.mov` files is a comparison of two clocks. `apng` has no such field, goes
through `ExporterImageSequence.swift` rather than `ExportWriter`, and came back
byte-identical across processes every time. H.264 is not deterministic at all
(measured: three exports of one project, 2,638 / 2,625 / 2,638 bytes), which is
VideoToolbox's rate control and not a defect — it is the reason the cancel
scenario, which makes no byte claim, is the only place this script uses it. The
ProRes 4444 row's own claims are `tools/proof/phase7_proof.py`'s, over MCP,
where `ffprobe` can read the pixel format.

**Two instruments this script builds, both declared here rather than buried.**

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Geometry, in POINTS, from the app's layout constants. Section 5 is the only
# one that photographs anything, so this list is short.

WIDTH = 1440
# The Document tab's window. It has to be tall enough that the Appearance
# section's open body AND the Markers section under it are both inside the
# inspector's scroll view in BOTH renders — at the default 862 the note pushes
# the Background row off the bottom, so nothing below it moves and the shift
# this section measures would come back zero for the wrong reason. Measured at
# 862 (the Background row is clipped) and at 1200 (everything fits, and the
# solve is exact).
HEIGHT = 1200

TOOLBAR = 44             # DS.toolbarHeight
INSPECTOR_W = 304        # DS.panelWidth
SCROLLER_W = 16          # AppKit's legacy scroller, pinned by the harness
INSET = 10               # InspectorMetrics.inset
CONTROL_H = 22           # DS.controlHeight — one row
ROW_SPACING = 7          # InspectorMetrics.rowSpacing
SECTION_HEADER_H = 28    # InspectorMetrics.headerHeight

INSPECTOR_X = WIDTH - INSPECTOR_W                        # 1136
LABEL_X0 = INSPECTOR_X + INSET                           # 1146
CONTROL_X1 = INSPECTOR_X + INSPECTOR_W - INSET - SCROLLER_W

# The band the shift is solved over: the Markers section, which is the only
# thing BELOW Appearance in the Document tab (`DocumentPane.sections` is
# Summary, Canvas, Frame Rate, Appearance, Markers). It starts below the
# Appearance section's open body in both renders and ends well above the
# timeline, so a shift cannot be measured against content that was pushed out
# of the pane.
BELOW_Y0 = 615
BELOW_H = 135
# What "an exact shift" means: the winner must leave NO row of the band
# unexplained, and the runner-up must be far worse — the half that says a
# number was measured and not merely preferred. (`phase6_chrome.py`'s rule,
# and its numbers.)
SHIFT_MARGIN = 40
# Where the Document summary line is, the one thing above the Appearance
# section that a background change legitimately redraws ("Black" against
# "Black · 50%").
SUMMARY_Y0, SUMMARY_H = 222, 22
# Everything above this belongs to the sections ABOVE Appearance, which a note
# inside Appearance must not move.
ABOVE_Y1 = 500
# A patch of the toolbar's Export button, which is an `AccentButton` filled
# with `DS.accent` — the same ink `InspectorNoteLabel` draws its text in. No
# colour is written down anywhere in this file: the note's ink is compared
# against this rectangle's, measured in the very render being read, so the
# check holds whatever the person at the machine chose in System Settings.
#
# It sits in the flat run between the button's leading edge (x 1334 pt,
# measured) and its share glyph, NOT across the middle — a rectangle spanning
# the button's whole width is 30 % icon and label, and a modal over that is a
# modal over the fill only by luck. Section 5 scores the "is this inside a flat
# fill" question rather than assuming it.
ACCENT_X0, ACCENT_Y0, ACCENT_W, ACCENT_H = 1336, 15, 10, 14

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Packages, by hand (spec §5.2). A `.framejob` is a directory holding a
# `project.json`, so nothing here loads asynchronously and every render is
# deterministic. Every fixture is a SHAPE card with no media at all: a shape
# clip needs no decode, gives the Document tab everything it draws, and
# exports through `CompositionBuilder`'s placeholder track — which is what
    # …and a SECOND canvas height, because the placement is a FRACTION of it:
    # one height can only ever say where the box landed, and two say whether it
    # SCALES. 360 is exactly the height at which `BURN_IN_Y_FRACTION` x height
    # and a hard-coded 158.4 coincide, so a proof written against 360 alone
    # would pass against a constant — which is not a hypothetical: this script
    # was accidentally run against a build carrying that very constant (see the
    # header), where the 360 fixture drew a burn-in in the right place and the
    # taller one put it at 0.646 of the frame.
    "tall": dict(width=1280, height=720, seconds=1),
    # 4 — the queue. `card` is the fast one (a 320x180 second of shape) and
    # `long` is the only slow one in the file: the cancel scenario needs an
    # export still running when the cancel is asked for.
    "long": dict(width=1920, height=1080, seconds=25),
    # 5 — the Document tab. Two OPAQUE backgrounds, so that "a background
    # changed" and "the canvas went translucent" can be told apart; one
    # translucent; and the two sides of the 0.995 threshold.
    "doc-black": dict(width=1920, height=1080, seconds=5, background=BLACK),
    "doc-white": dict(width=1920, height=1080, seconds=5, background=WHITE),
    "doc-half": dict(width=1920, height=1080, seconds=5, background=[0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.5]),
    "doc-a99": dict(width=1920, height=1080, seconds=5, background=[0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.99]),
    "doc-a999": dict(width=1920, height=1080, seconds=5, background=[0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.999]),
}


def write_package(name, spec):
    path = os.path.join(WORK, "p7-" + name + ".framejob")

content.content:
# 5. The Document tab's transparency note — the one photograph.
    print("\n5. the Document tab's transparency note")
    renders = {
        tag: render(harness, packages[tag], png(tag))
        for tag in ("doc-black", "doc-white", "doc-half", "doc-a99", "doc-a999")
    }
    images = LazyImages(renders)
    black = images["doc-black"]
    scale = black.scale
    inspector = Rect("the inspector", INSPECTOR_X, 0, INSPECTOR_W, HEIGHT)
    summary = Rect("the Document summary line", LABEL_X0, SUMMARY_Y0,
                   CONTROL_X1 - LABEL_X0, SUMMARY_H)
    above = Rect("everything above the Appearance section", INSPECTOR_X, 0, INSPECTOR_W,
                 ABOVE_Y1)
    band = Rect("the Markers section under Appearance", INSPECTOR_X, BELOW_Y0, INSPECTOR_W,
                BELOW_H)

    opaque_diff = inside(changed_pixels(black, images["doc-white"]), inspector, scale)
    print(f"\n   two OPAQUE canvases (black against white): {len(opaque_diff)} changed "
          f"pixels in the inspector, in {len(clusters(opaque_diff))} clusters:")
    print(describe(clusters(opaque_diff), scale))
    opaque_shift = shift_match(black, images["doc-white"], band)
    check("changing an opaque background changes the summary line and the swatch and MOVES "
          "NOTHING — the control this section needs, because without it a shift measured "
          "below could be any background change rather than the note",
          bool(opaque_diff) and opaque_shift[0] == (0, 0)
          and opaque_shift[1][0] >= SHIFT_MARGIN,
          f"the winning shift is {opaque_shift[0][1]} pt with {opaque_shift[0][0]} "
          f"mismatched rows; the runner-up is {opaque_shift[1][1]} pt with "
          f"{opaque_shift[1][0]}")

    note_diff = inside(changed_pixels(black, images["doc-half"]), inspector, scale)
    print(f"\n   opaque against TRANSLUCENT: {len(note_diff)} changed pixels in the "
          f"inspector, in {len(clusters(note_diff))} clusters:")
    print(describe(clusters(note_diff), scale))
    scores = shift_match(black, images["doc-half"], band)
    shift = scores[0][1]
    check("a TRANSLUCENT canvas pushes everything below the Appearance section DOWN by an "
          "exact whole number of points — every row of the band explained, and the "
          "runner-up far worse, which is what says the number was measured and not "
          "preferred",
          scores[0][0] == 0 and scores[0][1] > 0 and scores[1][0] >= SHIFT_MARGIN,
          f"{shift} pt with {scores[0][0]} mismatched rows of "
          f"{int(BELOW_H * scale)}; runner-up {scores[1][1]} pt with {scores[1][0]}")
    check(f"…and what was inserted is ONE LABEL row, not a control row and not a section: "
          f"the growth is more than the stack's own row spacing ({ROW_SPACING} pt) and less "
          f"than a control row and its spacing ({CONTROL_H + ROW_SPACING} pt), which is "
          f"exactly what an `InspectorNoteLabel` at 11 pt costs",
          ROW_SPACING < shift < CONTROL_H + ROW_SPACING,
          f"{shift} pt = {ROW_SPACING} pt of spacing + a {shift - ROW_SPACING} pt label")
    # Re-measured in place 2026-09-23 (road map 9 phase 3b, spec §11 CI-9):
    # the Appearance section's Reset now shows only while it differs from
    # its default (opaque black), so the translucent render ALSO draws that
    # button in the section's header — the one cluster of the diff exactly
    # one control tall that straddles `ABOVE_Y1`. It is excused here, and the
    # note's row below is found under it rather than at it.
    resets = [Rect("the Appearance section's Reset", b[0] / scale, b[1] / scale,
                   (b[2] + 1 - b[0]) / scale, (b[3] + 1 - b[1]) / scale)
              for b in clusters(note_diff)
              if abs((b[3] + 1 - b[1]) / scale - CONTROL_H) <= 0.5
              and b[1] < ABOVE_Y1 * scale <= b[3]]
    print("      " + ("; ".join(str(r) for r in resets) or "no Reset button in the diff"))
    stray = outside(inside(note_diff, above, scale), [summary] + resets, scale)
    check("nothing above the Appearance section moved or redrew except the Document "
          "summary, which legitimately reads \"Black · 50%\" instead of \"Black\" — so the "
          "note is INSIDE the section whose value it is about, and the Canvas and Frame "
          "Rate sections above it were not touched",
          bool(inside(note_diff, summary, scale)) and not stray,
          f"{summary}" if not stray else f"{len(stray)} px elsewhere above y {ABOVE_Y1} pt:\n"
          + describe(clusters(stray), scale))

    # The note's own row, located from the pixels rather than written down: the
    # first row below the sections above that the two renders disagree about is
    # where the Appearance section's content begins, and the note is the
    # `shift - ROW_SPACING` points from there.
    below_top = [p for p in outside(note_diff, resets, scale) if p[1] >= ABOVE_Y1 * scale]
    content_top = min((p[1] for p in below_top), default=0) / scale
    note_row = Rect("the note row", LABEL_X0, content_top, CONTROL_X1 - LABEL_X0,
                    max(shift - ROW_SPACING, 1))
    accent_patch = Rect("the Export button's fill", ACCENT_X0, ACCENT_Y0, ACCENT_W, ACCENT_H)
    accent, accent_count, accent_total = modal_pixel(images["doc-half"], accent_patch)
    check("the accent probe lands inside a flat fill — the toolbar's Export button is an "
          "`AccentButton` painted in `DS.accent`, and this rectangle has to be INSIDE it "
          "for the comparison below to mean anything",
          accent is not None and accent_count > 0.75 * max(accent_total, 1),
          f"{accent} covers {accent_count}/{accent_total} px of {accent_patch}")
    background, _, _ = modal_pixel(images["doc-half"], note_row)
    ink, ink_count, _ = modal_pixel(images["doc-half"], note_row, exclude={background})
    check("the note is drawn in the ACCENT — its ink is the same pixel as the Export "
          "button's fill, measured in the same render, so this holds whatever colour the "
          "person at the machine chose in System Settings and no colour is written down "
          "here", ink is not None and accent is not None and ink == accent,
          f"{note_row}: ink {ink} ({ink_count} px) against the button's {accent}")
    opaque_ink, _, _ = modal_pixel(
        images["doc-black"], note_row,
        exclude={modal_pixel(images["doc-black"], note_row)[0]})
    check("…and the same band of the OPAQUE render holds a different ink entirely — it is "

## C6a — the Export Queue's memory limit and the sheet's estimate

### Record

**Decision.** CX-18, recorded before the code (`designs/spec/11-decisions/codec-export.md`;
amends #326's `queued` answer). The queue stays one job at a time; a bundled-encoder export
(settings with a `writer`) is booked in `ExportEncoderLedger` from just before its
`Exporter.export` call to its finish — the queue's running job and every Export… progress
sheet's; a queued encoder job is admitted when nothing is booked or the booked costs and its
own fit a quarter of physical memory; a held job is passed over by a later admitted one and
says why; a sheet is counted, never held; a writer row with no measured entry (C5's alpha row
until it is measured) costs the whole budget. No format bump, op or `rc_*`.

**What landed.**
- `app/Sources/ExportEncoderCosts.swift` (new): `ExportEncoderKey` (row, AV1 speed, bit
  depth), `ExportEncoderFigure` (1080p and 4K, proportional below 1080p, linear above),
  `ExportTimeEntry`, the `memory` and `time` tables with their sources, `memoryBytes`,
  `estimatedSeconds`, `estimateText` and `sheetLine`.
- `app/Sources/ExportEncoderLedger.swift` (new): the shared main-thread ledger, its
  notification, the budget (physical / 4), the admission rule, the held sentence, `begin`
  and `end`.
- `ExportQueueController.swift`: admission through the ledger with pass-over, each held
  job's `message`, the ledger observer re-running `start()`, `begin` before
  `exporter.export` in `launch`, and `finished` clearing its token before `end`.
- `ExportProgressSheetController.swift`: `begin` in `viewDidAppear` before `export`; `end`
  first in `finished` and in `deinit`, the token cleared first.
- `ExportQueueWindowController.swift`: `ExportQueueRowView.status(_:)` internal, `.waiting`
  reading `job.message ?? "Waiting"`.
- `ExportSheetResolve.swift`: the summary's second line (two lines added; 581).
- `ExportSheetController.swift`: the hint's queue sentence names the memory wait.
- `AgentServer+ExportStatus.swift`: `queued` adds `waiting`; `queued` and `running` add
  `estimated_seconds`. `AgentCatalog+Render.swift`: `export`'s and `export_status`'s text.
- Spec §7.4, §7.8, §7.9a; the guide's export page; `app/CLAUDE.md`'s map;
  `tools/proof/README.md`.

**The measurement** (`RC_PROOF_APP=release python3 tools/proof/encoder_memory_measure.py`,
2026-10-28, Release built from the tree before any C6a code, Apple M2 Max, 96 GiB; one fresh
instance per row; AV.mov twice, 10 s, 300 frames; Δ = peak − baseline RSS sampled every
0.1 s; seconds the done answer's `elapsed`; load the 1-minute average at the export's start).
**Taken on a shared machine**: the C5 lane (`~/devel/framejob-codecs`) was building and
running proofs at the same time, which is why the load rose from about 9 in the first half
to about 33 in the second. The JSON is `tools/proof/work/encoder-memory/2026-10-28/memory.json`
(gitignored). Every instance log was free of `Frame Job: ` lines.

`ExportEncoderCosts.memory` is the Δ bytes column, transcribed exactly; `time`'s per-frame
seconds are each row's `seconds / 300`, `setupSeconds` 0. What the figures are and are not:
- The picture is AV.mov (640 × 360) scaled to the canvas, which is easy to encode: these
  speeds are far above the spike's `real8` (SVT preset 6 at about 75 fps at 1080p, here
  about 144 fps including the composition), and the per-frame time carries the
  composition, the loudness pass and the container besides the encoder. The memory is the
  encoder's lookahead and reference buffers at the size, which depend on the picture far
  less, and the 1080p AV1 figures sit beside the spike's 1,149–1,567 MB maximum RSS.
- One run each, the samples 13–81 per export (0.1 s apart); a peak between samples is
  missed, so a figure can be low by a sample's worth of growth.
- The 4K `smaller` rows were slower than `balanced` on `av1` (8.043 against 8.403 s) under
  very different loads (34.8 against 8.8): the time figures are PROVISIONAL, and C6b owes
  4K on every row and the idle three-run speeds that replace them.
- What the limit means on real Macs: a quarter of 32 GiB (8 GiB) admits one AV1 job at 4K
  at any speed, three at 1080p Balanced, and seven VP9 SDR jobs at 4K; on 16 GiB (4 GiB) one
  AV1 4K job always runs alone (CX-18 (5)) and nothing joins it. Since the queue runs one
  job at a time, the hold bites only beside Export… sheets.

**The probe needs no instance.** The spec had the probe open packages the proof saved over
MCP, so `--probe` would have needed an app; instead `encoder_limit_probe.swift` builds A1's
and W9's projects in process from AV.mov, as `webm_readers_probe.swift` builds A1's, and
`--probe` runs with no app at all. Q5's empty-project refusals use A1's `av1` settings over
an empty handle, because the core resolves no settings for an empty range.

**Proof** (2026-10-28, the same shared machine, load 30–100 from the C5 lane).
- `make gate`: PASS on the second attempt. The first stopped at `test` on
  `graphic/tests/path.rs`'s `a_path_over_the_memos_cost_bound_measures_the_same_twice` ("over
  the 250 ms budget at frame 7") with a load average near 100. No graphic file changed; the
  re-run passed `test` (155 s) and `app` (160 s), the earlier steps skipped as unchanged.
- `RC_PROOF_APP=release python3 tools/proof/encoder_limit_proof.py`: **17/17**.
  - Q1: the sheet (W9 as `av1` Smaller, 3,600 frames at 1080p) cost 2,419,654,656 bytes and
    the budget was set equal to it. A (`av1` Balanced, A1, 241,443,726) was held: "Waiting
    for memory: AV1 and VP9 exports running now hold about 2.3 GB of the 2.3 GB this Mac
    allows them, and this one needs about 0.2 GB." B ran and finished at sequence 5–61 and C
    at 62–136. The sheet finished at 137, A launched at 137 inside the sheet's `end`, and A
    finished at 147.
  - Q3, at 1 TiB: A was running at sequence 3 and the sheet finished at 13.
  - Q5: the ledger was empty at all five points.
  - S1 read "640 × 360 · 30 fps · 00:00:05:00\nEstimated time: about 5 s".
  - X1's `estimated_seconds` was 0, as the table gives: 150 frames at 640 × 360 come to

- `ExportQueueController.swift` · `ExportQueueWindowController.swift` — the
  controller has NO AppKit in it so a probe can drive it; one job at a time on
  the MAIN thread with a fresh `Exporter` each (two concurrent ones deadlock);
  `mediaURLs()` AND the document's compiled graphics (`Job.graphics`)
  captured at ENQUEUE. The agent's `export` enqueues here too (spec §11
  #326): its job shows in the window with its progress and Cancel, and
  `export_status` / `cancel_export` read and cancel it by the job's id. A
  bundled-encoder job waits while `ExportEncoderLedger` does not admit it
  (spec §11 CX-18): `start()` launches the first waiting job the ledger
  admits, passing over a held one, sets each held job's `message` to the
  ledger's sentence, and re-runs on the ledger's notification; `launch`
  books BEFORE `exporter.export` (an early refusal finishes inside it) and
  `finished` takes its token, clears it, THEN ends it (the end's post can
  launch and book the next job).
- `ExportEncoderCosts.swift` · `ExportEncoderLedger.swift` — Foundation only
  (spec §11 CX-18). Costs: `ExportEncoderKey` (row, AV1 speed, bit depth),
  the measured resident peak (`memory`) and per-frame time (`time`) at 1080p
  and 4K, each with its source, read at an export's pixels; the sheet's
  estimate (`sheetLine`). Replacing a figure is a table edit (C6b owes the
  time constants). Ledger: the app-wide main-thread account the queue and
  every `ExportProgressSheetController` book into (the sheet in
  `viewDidAppear` before `export`, ended in `finished` and `deinit`), its
  budget a quarter of physical memory, the admission rule and the held
  sentence; a writer row with no entry costs the whole budget.

def shift_match(top, bottom, band, limit=60):
    """How far DOWN `bottom` is `top`, measured over `band`.

    Walks every whole-point shift and counts the rows of `band` that do not
    match; the winner is the growth, in points, and the runner-up is what says
    the winner was measured rather than preferred. (`phase6_chrome.py`'s, with
    a shorter limit — the only thing that can move here is one label row.)"""
    scale = bottom.scale
    ch = bottom.channels
    x0, x1 = int(band.x0 * scale) * ch, int(band.x1 * scale) * ch
    y0, y1 = int(band.y0 * scale), int(band.y1 * scale)
    scores = []
    for points in range(limit):
        offset = int(points * scale)
        if y0 - offset < 0:
            break
        mismatch = sum(
            1 for y in range(y0, y1)
            if bottom.rows[y][x0:x1] != top.rows[y - offset][x0:x1])
        scores.append((mismatch, points))
    scores.sort()
    return scores


def changed_row_band(a_path, b_path):
    """The rows two same-sized PNGs disagree about, as
    `(top, bottom, height, x0, x1, width)` in PIXELS, or None when they agree.

    Used on the FIRST FRAME of two APNG exports — an animated PNG's default
    image is an ordinary PNG, so `decode_png` reads it with no new instrument —
    to find where the timecode burn-in landed. It is a row band rather than a
    rectangle because that is the whole of the claim: the burn-in's placement is
    a fraction of the canvas HEIGHT.
    """
    wa, ha, ch, rows_a = decode_png(a_path)
    wb, hb, _, rows_b = decode_png(b_path)
    if (wa, ha) != (wb, hb):
        return None
    rows = [y for y in range(ha) if rows_a[y] != rows_b[y]]
    if not rows:
        return None
    xs = set()
    for y in rows:
        ra, rb = rows_a[y], rows_b[y]
        x = int.from_bytes(ra, "big") ^ int.from_bytes(rb, "big")
        xb = x.to_bytes(len(ra), "big")
        for m in re.finditer(rb"[^\x00]+", xb):
            xs.add(m.start() // ch)
            xs.add((m.end() - 1) // ch)
    return min(rows), max(rows), ha, min(xs), max(xs), wa


def modal_pixel(image, rect, exclude=()):

def render(binary, package, out, height=HEIGHT):
    """One render of the DOCUMENT tab, with the harness's arguments in the
    order every earlier chrome script depends on. This script adds no argument
    to the renderer at all — `doc.appearance` is built `defaultExpanded: true`,
    so phase 3's `expandSections` is not needed either."""
    args = [
        binary, package, out, "light", str(WIDTH), str(height), "0", "0", "1",
        "document", "-", "-",
    ]
    result = subprocess.run(args, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if result.returncode != 0 or not os.path.exists(out):
        sys.stderr.write(result.stdout + result.stderr)
        sys.exit(f"render failed for {package}")
    # `Harness.png` writes one line to stderr when two consecutive captures
    # never came back equal — the layout was still moving when it gave up, and
    # every byte comparison would then be measuring a race instead of the
    # feature. Collected rather than ignored, and scored at the end.
    if result.stderr.strip():
        WARNINGS.append(f"{os.path.basename(out)}: {result.stderr.strip()}")
    return out

### Fix pass 1 (2026-10-28): the held sentence in the tooltip, the review's nits, two residues

**The should-fix: the held sentence was unreadable.** The queue row's status label is one
mono line that truncates its tail, so at the window's width the held sentence lost its GB
figures, and the tooltip did not carry them either. `ExportQueueRowView.toolTip(for:)` now
ends with `job.message` while the job waits, so the whole sentence is a hover away. The row
stays one line: its height is fixed (52 pt) and a wrapped status label in its stack would
need its own width solving, so wrapping was not taken. The guide's export page says what the
window shows: one line, cut with "…" where it does not fit, and the whole sentence in the
tooltip; spec §7.8 says the same.

**The nits, all fixed (the owner's residue rule).**
1. `ExportEncoderCosts.estimatedSeconds` answers nil when `sequenceFrameCount` is nil (a rate
   that cannot be stepped), so the sheet shows no estimate line and `export_status` has no
   `estimated_seconds`, where before it estimated 0 frames as "about 5 s" and 0. CX-18 (9)
   and §7.8 say so.
2. `encoder_memory_measure.py` fails a case whose baseline RSS cannot be read, instead of
   recording the whole peak as its delta.
3. `docs/manual-checks.md` SE-20: the sheet's estimate line on each AV1 and VP9 choice, and
   a held queue row and its tooltip, in both appearances.

**The proof.** Q4 also reads `toolTip(for:)`: A's ends with the whole sentence, and C's has
no "Waiting for memory" line. E3 also takes `av1` at fps 0/1 (no frame count): no line, no
seconds. Two mutants were added, one per new branch: `tip-drops-hold` (Q4) and
`estimate-no-count` (E3).

**Residue 1: `phase7_chrome.py`'s four Document-pane failures, fixed in the instrument.**
Section 5 solves the translucent note's shift over a band written down in points. The
summary's Colour row (HD-2) and the Canvas section's Dynamic Range and Blending rows (HD-2,
HD-16) moved the Appearance section down about 95 pt, so the band (y 615) lay across the
Background swatch, which a background change redraws. The opaque control's winning shift
then left 35 rows unexplained. The note row was found at the Appearance header's Reset (y
584) instead of under it, and read white ink. Every check that read the band failed, on
main as on C6a. The constants were re-measured from the script's own renders: `ABOVE_Y1`
500 → 595, which cuts through the Reset (584–606 pt), so the Reset is recognised and
excused; `BELOW_Y0` 615 → 660, the rows under the Background row (Timecode, Fit, Markers).
Markers alone is now too short to clear `SHIFT_MARGIN` in the opaque control: a band at 724
gave a runner-up of 23 rows against the 40 required. At 660 the translucent render's
runner-up is 100 rows and the control's 74. No app file changed for this.

**Residue 2: `graphic/tests/path.rs`'s timing budget, made robust.** R2, R4 and R5 ran their
render under the 250 ms preview budget as the engine's wall-clock call deadline. A load
average near 100 stretched R4's wall time past it, and the engine interrupted the call ("over
the 250 ms budget at frame 7"). That is a flaky gate, not a slow path. `timed` now runs the
call under a 10 s deadline (`HANG_MS`, which only a hang trips) and asserts the calling
thread's CPU time (`clock_gettime_nsec_np(CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID)`; the engine is
`thread_local!`, so the render runs on that thread) under `BUDGET_MS`. It is still a real
check. The claim is what the path costs to measure, and CPU time counts exactly that work
while leaving out the time a busy host kept the thread off a core. On an idle host the two
agree. At a load average of 94, R2 took 17.3 ms of CPU (17.8 wall) and R4 68.4 ms (68.5
wall). A regression that made the memo re-measure, or made the measuring slower, still
fails it at the same 250 ms.

**Verification.**
EOF
echo ok
input.description: Append fix pass record to road map

# C6a fix notes, pass 1

Worktree `~/devel/framejob-lane-c` (branch `lane-c`). Nothing was committed, pushed or merged. The only app instances I launched were the proofs' own; each proof stopped its instances. At the end, only the C5 lane's instance was running.

## Findings (05-review.md)
1. **should-fix: the held sentence is truncated. FIXED.**
   - `ExportQueueRowView.toolTip(for:)` (`app/Sources/ExportQueueWindowController.swift`) appends `job.message` while `job.state == .waiting`, so the whole sentence is a hover away.
   - The row stays one line. Its height is fixed at 52 pt, and wrapping a status label inside its stack would need its own width solving. RULING-1 made wrapping optional, so I did not take it.
   - `docs/guide/export.md` now says exactly what the window shows: the status is one line and ends in "…" where the sentence does not fit; the tooltip ends with the whole sentence. The tooltip bullet now lists the sentence.
   - Spec §7.8 says the same.
2. **nit: a nil `sequenceFrameCount` gives an estimate. FIXED.** `ExportEncoderCosts.estimatedSeconds` returns nil when there is no frame count. As a result:
   - the sheet shows no estimate line;
   - `estimated_seconds` is absent. The catalog documents the key as something `queued` and `running` "add", so absence fits it, and the catalog text was not changed.
   - CX-18 (9) and §7.8 say so.
3. **nit: a failed baseline read. FIXED.** In `encoder_memory_measure.py`, a baseline of None sets the row's `error` and returns, so the case fails and the script exits 1. The delta is now `peak − baseline`, with no `or 0`. The README says so.
4. **nit: no manual-checks row. FIXED.** I added `docs/manual-checks.md` **SE-20**, which covers:
   - the sheet's estimate line on each AV1 and VP9 choice, and its absence on H.264;
   - a held queue row at the opening width, its tooltip, and the pass-over;
   - both appearances.
   - Note: the C5 lane may also add an SE-20. Whoever merges second should renumber.

## RULING-1 item 3: pre-existing residue (both fixed; no issue filed)
- **`phase7_chrome.py`, 75/79 → 79/79. Fixed in the instrument.**
  - Cause: section 5 measures over constants written in points. The summary's Colour row (HD-2) and the Canvas section's Dynamic Range and Blending rows (HD-2, HD-16) moved the Appearance section down about 95 pt.
  - Effect: the band at y 615 lay across the Background swatch, which the black and white renders draw differently, so the opaque control had 35 unexplained rows. The note row was found at the Reset button (y 584), read white ink, and every check that reads the band failed.
  - Fix: I re-measured from the script's own renders.
    - `ABOVE_Y1` 500 → 595. It now cuts through the Reset at 584–606 pt, so the Reset is excused as the code intends.
    - `BELOW_Y0` 615 → 660, the rows under the Background row (Timecode, Fit, Markers).
  - Why not Markers alone at 724: its runner-up in the opaque control was 23 rows, under `SHIFT_MARGIN` 40. At 660 the runner-ups are 74 (opaque control) and 100 (translucent).
  - The comments carry the re-measurement. No app file changed.
- **`graphic/tests/path.rs` timing budget. Made robust.**
  - What failed: the 250 ms budget was the engine's wall-clock call deadline, so under load the engine interrupted R4 with "over the 250 ms budget".
  - New form: `timed` runs the call under `HANG_MS` = 10 s, which only a hang trips. It asserts the calling thread's CPU time (`clock_gettime_nsec_np(CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID)`; the engine is `thread_local!`) under `BUDGET_MS`, and prints the wall time beside it.
  - Why it is still a real check: it measures the work the path costs and leaves out the time a busy host kept the thread off a core. It has the same 250 ms threshold, and on an idle host CPU and wall time agree. At a load of 94: R2 took 17.3 ms CPU (17.8 wall) and R4 68.4 ms CPU (68.5 wall).
  - The `unsafe` extern is in a test; `forbid(unsafe_code)` covers only `lib.rs`.
- Both are recorded in `designs/codec-export.md`, in "## C6a" → "### Fix pass 1".

## Proof changes
- **Q4** also checks `ExportQueueRowView.toolTip(for:)`: A's tooltip ends with `"\n" + held`, and C's has no "Waiting for memory".
- **E3** also covers `av1` at fps [0, 1] (`sequenceFrameCount` nil): no frames, no line, no seconds. The probe's `settings(...)` gained an `fps:` parameter.
- **Two new mutants**, one per new branch:
  - `tip-drops-hold` → Q4;
  - `estimate-no-count` → E3.
- The docstring and `tools/proof/README.md` were updated: twelve mutants, Q4's tooltip, E3's unstepped case, and the measure script's baseline failure.

## Verification
- **Targeted**
  - `make typecheck`: exit 0. 0 errors, exactly the 4 baseline warnings (CompositionBuilder ×2, +Orientation, Exporter).
  - `python3 tools/proof/swift_build.py typecheck tools/proof/encoder_limit_probe.swift`: exit 0.
  - `python3 tools/proof/encoder_limit_proof.py --probe`: exit 0, `scores: 13/13`.
    - E3 answered `{"line": null, "seconds": null, "unsteppedFrames": null, "unsteppedLine": null, "unsteppedSeconds": null}`.
    - Q4: A's tooltip is `…/q1-a.mp4\nMP4 · 640 × 360 · 30 fps\nWaiting for memory: … needs about 0.2 GB.`
  - Mutants `tip-drops-hold`, `estimate-no-count` and `row-says-waiting`: each exit 1, `MUTANT CAUGHT`, failing exactly its named row.
    - `estimate-no-count`'s E3 showed `"unsteppedLine": "Estimated time: about 5 s", "unsteppedSeconds": 0`.
    - I did not re-run the other nine mutants: their anchors and rows are unchanged.
  - `cd graphic && cargo fmt && cargo test --release --test path -- --nocapture`: exit 0, 6 passed (load 94.73).
  - `python3 tools/proof/spec_index_proof.py`: exit 0, 210/210. I updated three Lines cells: §7.8 616, codec-export.md 573, folder 14324.
- **Full**
  - `python3 tools/proof/phase7_chrome.py`, before the fix (with this pass's Swift in): 75/79, the same four Document-pane failures and the queue sections passing. After the fix: exit 0, **79/79**.
  - `make gate`: exit 0, `gate: PASS 386s`. names 1 s, typecheck 19 s, fmt 4 s, lint 2 s, test 171 s, app 187 s.
  - `RC_PROOF_APP=release python3 tools/proof/encoder_limit_proof.py`: exit 0, `scores: 17/17`.
    - S1: `'640 × 360 · 30 fps · 00:00:05:00\nEstimated time: about 5 s'`.
    - X1: estimated_seconds 0 (want 0).
    - Z1: complaints [].
  - `RC_PROOF_APP=release python3 tools/proof/export_status_proof.py`: exit 0, `9/9`, Z1 [].
  - `make gate` again after the road map record was written (an `.md` input): exit 0. names pass; the other steps skipped as unchanged.
